core_obligations: Finite order case: by the general principle following the definition of a thickening it suffices to treat a first order thickening, and then the exact sequence for that case shows that it is enough that H^1(X, I)[n], H^1(X, I)/n and H^2(X, I)[n] all vanish; these vanish because multiplication by n on the O_X-module I is an isomorphism since n is invertible in O_X (proof lines 640-648).

General case setup: for an arbitrary thickening let I contained in O_{X'} be the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf cutting out X, so that there is a short exact sequence of abelian groups 0 -> (1 + I)^* -> O_{X'}^* -> O_X^* -> 0, and take its long exact cohomology sequence, which is the sequence of the first order lemma with H^i(X, I) systematically replaced by H^i(X, (1 + I)^*) (proof lines 652-660).

General case conclusion: it therefore suffices to show that raising to the nth power is an isomorphism of (1 + I)^*, which on sections over affine opens follows from the algebraic lifting lemma for nth roots (proof lines 661-664).
proof_roadmap: First proof, finite order case: reduce to a first order thickening and kill the three cohomology groups of the ideal sheaf using invertibility of n (proof lines 640-648).
Second proof, general case: introduce the ideal sheaf I of the thickening and the exponential sequence 0 -> (1 + I)^* -> O_{X'}^* -> O_X^* -> 0 (proof lines 652-657).

Note that the long exact sequence of that exponential sequence is the first-order sequence with H^i(X, I) replaced by H^i(X, (1 + I)^*), so the statement reduces to invertibility of the nth power map on (1 + I)^*, which is the cited algebraic fact (proof lines 658-664).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a thickening X contained in X' and an integer n invertible on X, the restriction map on n-torsion subgroups of the Picard groups is bijective (statement lines 634-636). The author gives two proofs, and the pair is instructive: the first reduces finite-order thickenings to the first-order case and then needs the vanishing of H^1(X, I)[n], H^1(X, I)/n and H^2(X, I)[n], all of which follow from multiplicativity by an invertible n on the ideal sheaf (proof lines 640-648); the second avoids the reduction by working with the group (1 + I)^* of units congruent to one, whose exponential sequence is the first-order exact sequence with the ideal sheaf replaced throughout by (1 + I)^*, so that only the invertibility of the nth power map has to be supplied algebraically (proof lines 652-664). The claim is H2: two short and logically distinct arguments over one exact sequence.
